findings.title: Interpolation before querySupportsSplitting bypasses the $__range guard
findings.body: runSplitQuery applies template variables to every target at line 299 before partitioning with querySupportsSplitting. applyTemplateVariables resolves $__range against the full request range and removes the token, so isQueryWithRangeVariable in querySupportsSplitting no longer detects these queries and they are split. Each time chunk then keeps the full-range duration (for example rate({...}[$__range]) becomes rate({...}[2d]) in every 1-day chunk), producing overlapping or double-counted results; these queries were previously left unsplit specifically to avoid that. Check the range variable on the raw expression before interpolation, or carry the original expression through to the guard.

findings.title: Targets are interpolated twice on the shard-splitting path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery maps every target through applyTemplateVariables here, and then each shard group calls runSplitQuery, which applies applyTemplateVariables again (querySplitting.ts:299). Template interpolation is not idempotent: a literal escaped dollar such as $$__range becomes $__range after the first pass and is substituted on the second, and variable values containing $ are re-expanded. The new test expecting 5 applyTemplateVariables calls (one initial plus four shard groups) asserts this double interpolation. Pass already-interpolated targets to the nested splitting call or add an option to skip interpolation there.

findings.title: Empty-after-interpolation targets are not filtered out
findings.body: The expr filter runs before applyTemplateVariables. A query whose whole expression is a variable (for example $query) passes the filter even when interpolation produces an empty string, so runSplitQuery can execute datasource.runQuery with an empty expr. On the shard path the same ordering in shardQuerySplitting.ts:50 lets such an empty target reach groupTargetsByQueryType; when it is later passed to runSplitQuery it is filtered out and can leave the grouped request list empty, causing the Math.max/undefined access in runSplitGroupedQueries to fail. Filter again after mapping, as the old shard code did, or map before filtering.
